0me2h9k5d83c13fsqa9gngsepk.value: Fish in a 48 m pond that wraps round at its edges. Each fish follows a leader, swims toward the most food it smells, eats, ages, has young when it has energy to spare, and dies when it runs out or grows old. Six herons hunt the nearest fish. The food grows back each tick.

a11upvlroql06539n0mbv0tbeg.value: Each tick, every fish's plan is made from the pond as it was, by a map over the school that only computes, so it runs on several threads at once: here on the browser's workers, compiled to native code on the machine's cores. Then the plans are carried out in turn, the herons strike, and the food grows. The text main beside this page is the same pond, run from the command line and timed against hand-written C in GAPS round 13.

af5rqur24q0dgfppi8uapokl4c.value: Credits: the school follows leaders as Craig Reynolds's boids steer (1987); food grows back as Pierre-Francois Verhulst's logistic growth (1838); random numbers by Stephen Park and Keith Miller's minimal standard generator (1988); the fish are kept with generational keys and a free list, as game engines keep their entities.
